header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lee Chen (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Lotus CTO), Evan Ross (Lotus ML), Sofia Alvarez (Lotus Security), Trevor Lim (Lotus Platform)
summary: Kickoff for Lotus Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered success criteria, security requirements (SOC2/KMS/VPC), network/connectivity plan, initial pilot scope (3 inference workloads), timelines for technical deep dive and benchmarks, and next steps to share onboarding plan, security questionnaire, and schedule deep dive.
topics: Network setup (VPC peering, proxies, IP allowlist)
Pilot scope: model choices, latency targets, cost tradeoffs
Technical deep dive and benchmarking plan
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick round of intros then we'll run through the onboarding plan.
[00:12] Maya (Lotus): Hi, Maya here, CTO. We're excited to get started.
[00:18] Evan (Lotus): Evan, lead ML. Focusing on inference accuracy and tail latency for our triage models.
[00:24] Sofia (Lotus): Sofia from security, I'll be driving compliance questions.
[00:28] Trevor (Lotus): Trevor, platform eng, I'll run network/setup.
[00:33] Jordan: Great. Priya from our SE team will do a short tech overview. Priya?
[00:38] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all. I'll go over the runtime, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and what we'll need for connectivity. Quick note: transcript may have some auto-capture typos.
[00:50] Priya: So, high level Redwood supports hosted API for quick ramps, dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and private/VPC for regulated workloads. For Lotus, given the compliance ask from Sofia, I think we should plan private or dedicated at the start.
[01:05] Sofia: We prefer customer-managed keys and audit logs. SOC2 is a must, and we have a FedRAMP-ish set of controls internally. How do you support KMS/HSM?
[01:16] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping for private deployments, and we can do HSM-backed options for enterprise Private. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM. I'll share the security document with specifics.
[01:28] Lee (Redwood CSM): From onboarding perspective we'll do a two-week prep, then a pilot window. Jordan will own the timeline.
[01:35] Jordan: Yup. Success criteria we heard from earlier: sub-200ms p50 for our short prompts, consistent throughput of ~60 rps for the triage workload, and data residency in us-west. Is that accurate?
[01:48] Evan: That's right, for the triage we need p95 under 350ms. There's also a heavier summarization job that's okay with higher latency but must be cost-effective.
[01:58] Maya: Timeline: we want pilot running within three weeks if possible. Security review will be the gating factor.
[02:06] Jordan: Understood. Let's walk through the network checklist so Trevor knows exactly what to provision.
[02:12] Trevor: Our infra team runs behind a corporate proxy, we need to know outbound IP ranges and whether TLS interception will break cert pinning. Also curious about VPC peering vs Private Link options.
[02:24] Priya: For VPC peering we provide a CIDR range to allow; for Private Link we'd provide endpoints. If proxy does TLS interception that can break mutual TLS to KMS — we recommend bypass for those flows. We'll include a one-page network guide.
[02:40] Sofia: Also need retention details and where logs live. Can you redact PII from logs?
[02:46] Priya: We can configure log retention and have options for PII minimization; default hosted logs are retained per plan, but for private we can push logs to your SIEM and control retention.
[02:58] Jordan: OK moving to pilot scope — Evan, you mentioned three workloads?
[03:02] Evan: Yes: 1) triage classifier short prompts (95% under 350ms target), 2) clinician note summarization (longer context, cost-sensitive), 3) semantic search embeddings for internal knowledge (throughput focused).
[03:18] Priya: For the summarization we may recommend larger context model with KV cache and batching settings, but that impacts cost. We'll propose quantization and batching configs per workload.
[03:30] Maya: On the contract side, curious about committed vs burst capacity pricing for Dedicated. We'll want visibility on unit economics.
[03:38] Jordan: We'll send a pricing sheet. Dedicated has monthly commits and a burst pool; we can model costs for your traffic patterns once you share representative traces.
[03:47] Evan: We'll prepare traces. Trevor, can you extract the RPC latencies and request sizes?
[03:51] Trevor: Yep, I'll pull that and share.
[03:54] [04:00] Priya: Technical deep dive options: we can run a 90-min session where we do a bench of your triage workload, show p50/p95, and iterate on batching/quantization. We can also do a live KV-cache demo.
[04:14] Maya: That would help. For security, what attestations do you have? SOC 2 type II? ISO?
[04:20] Lee: We have SOC 2 Type II and are pursuing ISO; I'll share the compliance pack.
[04:27] Sofia: I need the data flow diagram and the KMS integration doc. Also, who is the technical contact for vaults?
[04:33] Jordan: Priya will be SE contact; and Lee for compliance pack. Priya: noted.
[04:38] [05:00] Priya: A few gotchas: if you plan on TLS-inspecting traffic that touches KMS calls that will cause issues. Also proxy idle timeouts affect streaming responses. We'll document recommended firewall and idle timeout settings.
[05:14] Trevor: Good to know, we'll check proxy policies.
[05:18] Evan: On the embeddings/indexing piece — we already use a vector DB, do you have guidance on dimensionality and storage for embeddings produced by Redwood?
[05:26] Priya: We'll share best-practice mappings, but typical flow is 1536 or 1024 dims depending on model; we can output normalized vectors and give you batching guidance to keep throughput high.
[05:36] Maya: Who signs the DPA / security addendum? We'll need that early.
[05:42] Jordan: I'll route paperwork to your legal contact after we agree on the pilot scope.
[05:46] [06:00] Lee: Recap of timeline: Quick prep over next week to gather network and security artefacts, 90-min deep dive in week of 10/18, pilot window starting ~10/25. Does that align?
[06:12] Maya: That aligns, pending security review.
[06:16] Jordan: Great. Any blocking concerns?
[06:19] Sofia: Just the security questionnaire and some clarity on key management. Also need a list of Redwood sub-processors.
[06:26] Jordan: We'll include sub-processor list in the compliance pack.
[06:30] [07:00] Priya: For the benchmark we'll want a small test harness and sample dataset. Evan, if you can supply 200 representative requests we can replay them.
[07:10] Evan: We'll prepare that.
[07:13] Trevor: I'll share network diagram and current egress IPs.
[07:17] Jordan: Sound plan. Any final questions?
[07:20] Maya: No, just please include estimated cost for the summarization workload so we can budget.
[07:25] Jordan: Will do.
[07:28] [08:00] Priya: Quick note on observability — Console can show token-level cost and latency traces per route; we'll show dashboards in the deep dive.
[08:12] Evan: Great, helps to pinpoint regressions.
[08:15] [09:00] Jordan: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the onboarding plan, security pack, and calendar invites for the deep dive.
[09:08] Maya: Thanks.
[09:10] Evan: Thanks all.
[09:12] Sofia: Thanks.
[09:14] Trevor: Thanks.
[09:20] [End]
